From a reference to something you made

Construction skills

Choose the smallest technique that produces the effect. Most styles combine artwork, layout, and interaction.

Composition

Arrange first; decorate second.

Set the information order, alignment edges, and focal point before selecting effects.

  • Design principles — freeCodeCamp
  • Choosing Type roadmap

Try it: Rearrange the same title, paragraph, and image in two layouts. Explain where the eye goes first.

Shapes and illustration

Build a reusable shape vocabulary.

Use vector paths for maps, frames, ornaments, and icons. Keep stroke weights and perspective consistent.

  • Inkscape basic tutorial

Try it: Draw a frame, a divider, and a button shape with the same visual rules.

Collage and image layers

Keep the pieces editable.

Masks let you combine photographs and textures without permanently erasing their source layers.

  • GIMP layer masks
  • Photopea layer styles

Try it: Combine three original fragments, then export each moving element separately.

Textures and painting

Study light as well as grain.

A convincing material needs a coherent light direction, edge treatment, and level of detail at its final size.

  • Krita basic concepts
  • Krita brush texture
  • ambientCG materials
  • Poly Haven textures

Try it: Make a clean button and a weathered one. Preserve the same silhouette and label.

Motion and sound

Storyboard the sequence.

Plan anticipation, movement, arrival, and feedback. Place impact sounds at the contact point rather than at the start of the animation.

  • The 12 principles of animation
  • GSAP getting started
  • Audacity editing
  • Browser autoplay rules

Try it: Sketch three frames for a heavy door closing. Write where the hinge and impact sounds belong.

3D and rendered scenes

Choose a still render or a live scene.

A rendered background with separate interface layers can create depth without a fully real-time 3D environment.

  • Blender features and learning entry point
  • Blender and Three.js portfolio course — video

Try it: Model one simple panel, light it, and render it at its final display size before building a whole world.
